result.title: PolUR: Polarization Aware Multimodal Degradation Perception for Underwater Image Restoration
result.summary: Recovering high-quality images from degraded underwater observations is crucial for underwater exploration. Polarization observations show promise as an effective source of complementary physical cues for recovering target radiance under clear-water conditions. However, existing methods have yet to jointly model raw intensity information and polarization cues to enable image restoration driven by an understanding of mixed degradations (color casts, haze, and low light). To overcome these limitations, we propose PolUR, a unified multimodal language-driven framework that jointly uses polarization and RGB information to identify degradation types and severity levels through structured semantic instructions and enhances joint restoration representations under the guidance of degradation-aware semantic features to improve restoration robustness under mixed degradations. We further construct a new benchmark named MixPolar, which contains underwater images exhibiting real-world degradations and their corresponding degradation descriptions. MixPolar supports systematic evaluation of degradation perception, image restoration, and performance on downstream tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PolUR effectively integrates polarization and RGB information, achieving competitive performance in degradation perception and image restoration, while also demonstrating generalization capability and utility for downstream tasks.

AI.brief_summary: PolUR 提出结合偏振与 RGB 的多模态语言驱动框架，通过结构化语义指令识别水下退化的类型与严重程度，并以退化感知语义特征引导图像复原，同时构建 MixPolar 基准评测退化感知与复原。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将语言模型的退化语义特征作为引导信号调制复原表征，可供核查 LM 隐表示如何注入并影响视觉表征（与 latent 内容是否被真正使用、信息坍缩等问题相关），但论文本身不涉及推理期 latent 状态生成与停止决策。
